verdict.justification: Both deliverables correctly identify the crucial workspace governance constraint: that the 21-day notice period (record-r2) is the approved governing fact, while the 12-week/84-day period (proposal-r3) is unapproved. However, Deliverable B provides a much stronger, more practical automotive sourcing and negotiation strategy. Deliverable B realizes that by leveraging LPI's 2,500/month ramp-up capacity, LiIon can cover its entire ~5.5-month redevelopment need within the 84-day extension window via a Last-Time-Buy (LTB) bank of 4,200–5,400 sets, whereas Deliverable A insists LPI must stay and ship 800 sets/month all the way until April 30, 2027. Furthermore, Deliverable B solves the tooling catch-22 by proposing a 'mould-ahead' strategy (moulding all LTB plastic parts in the first four weeks and releasing the tools on Day 28 while electronics assembly continues to Day 84). In contrast, Deliverable A has an internal timeline contradiction in Section 5, claiming plastics will be ready locally by late Jan/Feb 2027 while also insisting LPI must keep the tooling to continue shipping complete lamps through April 2027. Deliverable B also shows stronger operational rigor by flagging the potential 'units vs. sets' ambiguity in the prompt (Section 9, X4).
